title: Check and checkmate
summary: When your king is attacked you must save it. Learn the three ways out of check, and how to give a checkmate that ends the game.

rules.title: Three ways out.
rules.text: Move the king, block the attack, or capture the attacker.

rules.title: Checkmate.
rules.text: In check with no way out: the game is over.

steps.title: What check means
steps.text: When a piece attacks the king, the king is in check. The player in check must get out of it on the very next move: nothing else is allowed. Here White's rook gives check along the eighth rank.
steps.narration: When your king is attacked, that's called check. You must fix it right away. You can't ignore it and do something else.

steps.title: What is check?
steps.text: When a piece attacks the king, the king is in **check**. You must get out of it right away, in one of three ways:
steps.narration: Check means the king is attacked. There are only three ways out: move the king, block the attack, or capture the attacker.

steps.title: Three ways out
steps.prompt: You're in check. You can move the king, block with the bishop, or capture the rook. Pick the best.
steps.hint: One way out also wins Black's rook.
steps.success: Capturing the checking piece is often the best way out. You escaped the check and won a rook.
steps.narration: There are three ways out of check: move the king, block the attack, or capture the attacker. Here you can do all three. Which one is best?

steps.title: Checkmate
steps.text: Checkmate is a check with no way out. The king cannot move to a safe square, nothing can block, and the attacker cannot be captured. Here Black's own pawns box the king in, and the rook's check cannot be stopped. Checkmate ends the game.
steps.narration: Checkmate is check with no escape. The king can't run, nobody can block, and the attacker can't be taken. That's the goal of the whole game.

steps.title: Pick the board
steps.question: Which one is checkmate?

options.why: Yes! The king is in check and its own pawns block every escape square.
Check, but the king can slip out to h7.
Not even check! Black has no legal moves, so this is stalemate: a draw.
Check, but nothing protects the queen, so the king simply takes it.

steps.narration: Look at all four boards. Only one of them is checkmate. Which one?

steps.title: Your first checkmate
steps.hint: Black's king is walled in by its own pawns. Attack it along the back rank.
steps.success: Rook to d8 is checkmate. The pawns on f7, g7 and h7 trap their own king.
steps.narration: Now you try. Black's king is hiding behind its pawns, but those pawns are also its prison. Find the rook move that ends the game.

steps.title: Queen and king together
steps.hint: Your king already covers g7 and h7. Check along the eighth rank.
steps.success: Queen to b8 is checkmate. The queen controls the whole back rank and your king guards the escape squares.
steps.narration: Your king is helping out here, guarding the squares in front of Black's king. Bring your queen in with check where nothing can stop her.

steps.title: Quick check
steps.question: Your king is in check. Which of these is NOT a way out?

options.text: Capture one of your opponent's other pieces
options.why: Unless that capture removes the attacker, the king is still in check. You must deal with the check itself.

options.text: Move the king to a safe square
options.why: That is one of the three ways out.

options.text: Put a piece between the king and the attacker
options.why: Blocking works against rooks, bishops and queens. It is one of the three ways out.
Removing the attacker is often the best way out of all.

steps.narration: Last question. Remember the three ways out of check. Which of these choices doesn't actually save your king?
